packages.purpose: Start with pre‑computed dense passage embeddings from a standard retriever (e.g., Contriever) and the query embedding from the same encoder. Augment each passage embedding with a document ID embedding (relative to the current retrieved set) and a sinusoidal passage‑position encoding to inject structural cues. Process the query and enriched passage embeddings jointly through a stack of Transformer encoder layers that use a hybrid attention mechanism: a shared full attention module for global interactions, and a dedicated masked attention module that restricts attention to passages from the same document, to consolidate intra‑document coherence. Optimize the model with a contrastive loss (InfoNCE) that uses the fixed original query embedding as an anchor, pulling the contextualized positive passage embedding closer and pushing negatives away. At inference, compute dot‑product similarity between the static query embedding and the updated passage embeddings, then rank passages in descending order of these scores.

Hybrid‑attention encoding: Feed the query and augmented passage embeddings into a Transformer encoder that applies shared full attention (global interactions) and dedicated masked attention (intra‑document interactions) in every layer, producing contextualized passage embeddings.

author_statements: hybrid attention mechanism: Combines shared full attention (global cross‑passage) and dedicated masked attention (intra‑document) in each Transformer layer to jointly model inter‑ and intra‑document dependencies.
shared full attention module: Standard multi‑head attention allowing query and all passages to attend to each other;

dedicated masked attention module: Masked multi‑head attention that restricts a passage to attend only to the query and to other passages from the same document, enabling fine‑grained coreference resolution and local coherence.
